Few professions shape daily life as visibly as civil engineering, and that is what first drew me to it. Growing up fascinated by how bridges, roads, and skylines shape the way people live, travel, and connect, I chose civil engineering as the place where problem-solving and creativity meet to turn ideas into infrastructure that serves entire communities. I am originally from Peru, and I hold a Master’s degree from a university ranked in the global top 500. Through my studies and professional experience, I have become especially interested in translating complex technical requirements into clear, buildable plans that balance safety, efficiency, and cost, while working across different disciplines to keep projects practical and dependable. One of my favourite memories was taking my family on a road trip, where we crossed a bridge I had helped deliver and my youngest recognised a pedestrian crossing point on a concrete platform; watching that moment live in the real world confirmed for me how engineering can quietly shape ordinary travel.

That interest deepened through practical delivery and project work. In one role, I needed to use a technique that was new to me, so I learned it within a couple of months and then began applying it independently in my own work. On another project, a recurring issue was repeatedly slowing the team down, so I put together a practical workaround that reduced the disruption and helped the work move forward more smoothly. Colleagues now and then come to me with questions in areas I have worked on before, and I value being able to help them move forward with clear, usable answers. I have also completed 2 projects with tangible outcomes, and one of them required sustained effort over an extended period, including extra time when setbacks delayed progress, until it was delivered properly.

Overall, I am eager to bring this combination of technical grounding, project experience, and commitment to a Civil Engineer role where I can contribute to infrastructure that serves people well for years to come.

Few things are more satisfying than taking raw materials and shaping them into something lasting, useful, and beautifully made. That is what drew me to carpentry: the chance to combine creativity with practical problem-solving and to build spaces and furniture that become part of people’s daily lives. One of my clearest memories is bringing my family to see a community project I had helped build, only for my youngest relative to run straight to a bench I had made and proudly call it “our family bench.” That moment stayed with me because it captured exactly what I value in this trade: the satisfaction of reading a space accurately, planning efficiently, and producing work that stands up to years of use. I am originally from Spain, and I hold a Master’s degree from a university ranked in the global top 100. Across my experience, I have completed 5 projects with tangible outcomes, each reinforcing my interest in work that is durable, practical, and closely tied to the people who use it.

My academic background and hands-on experience have given me a strong foundation for carpentry, and I have also seen how much I enjoy making work that is not only visually striking, but also reliable and useful. In one role, I needed to use a technique that was new to me, so I learned it within a couple of months and then began applying it independently in my own work. On another project, a recurring issue was repeatedly slowing the team down, so I put together a practical workaround that reduced the disruption and helped the work move forward more smoothly. Colleagues now and then come to me with questions in areas they know I have worked on before, and I value those moments because they reflect the collaborative side of the trade. I have also seen a long assignment through to completion when it ran into obstacles, putting in additional time where needed so that the final outcome was delivered properly.

These experiences have strengthened my commitment to carpentry and strengthened the way I approach planning, accuracy, and practical problem-solving. I am now eager to bring that approach to a role where I can contribute to well-made, durable, and useful work.

Order has always felt most meaningful to me when it connects people, products, and businesses in a practical, visible way. That is what drew me to logistics and why I am applying for a Logistics Coordinator role: I have always been energized by bringing order to fast-moving situations, and logistics felt like the right way to turn that instinct into work that keeps people, products, and businesses connected. Over time, that interest has grown into a clear professional direction: I want to contribute as a Logistics Coordinator by helping keep operations running smoothly, balancing multiple priorities, and supporting work that keeps the pace steady behind the scenes. Originally from Sri Lanka, I hold a Master’s degree from a university ranked in the global top 500, and across my work I have completed 5 projects with tangible outcomes.

My academic background gave me a structured foundation for planning, organisation, and communication, and I have also seen how much progress depends on staying focused on what is actually happening. In one role, I had to use a method that was completely new to me; within a few weeks I was applying it confidently, and soon after I was the person colleagues came to when they needed someone to walk them through it step by step. On another occasion, I noticed that the team was repeatedly losing time at the same handover point, so I introduced a simple adjustment to the process that reduced delays and saved time across the workflow. I also make a point of sharing information about my own work whenever teammates need it, whether that means clarifying status, passing on updates, or helping someone locate the next step in a task.

What keeps this career personal for me is how naturally it connects to everyday life. On a family road trip, we unexpectedly passed one of the regional warehouses I help support, and my family insisted we stop so I could show them “where all the planning happens.” Seeing them connect my behind-the-scenes work to products arriving in stores made the profession feel especially real and rewarding. I am now eager to bring that same sense of purpose, steady coordination, and practical focus to a Logistics Coordinator position where I can help keep operations running smoothly.
